headline: Recommended proposed amendments to Code of Ordinances Article 26-9, Demolition Review, for City Council consideration; approved Master Plan Subcommittee memorandum.
summary: Members recommended changes to the demolition review ordinance and approved a Master Plan subcommittee memorandum with editorial edits. They also discussed proposed zoning changes for nonconforming residential structures, which had no recorded vote, and a September 19, 2026 community visioning session.

Recommended to City Council the proposed amendments to Code of Ordinances Article 26-9, Demolition Review, all in favor.
Approved the Master Plan Subcommittee memorandum with the noted editorial amendments, all in favor.

Page 1 of 5 
 
HERITAGE COMMISSION 
Meeting Minutes - Draft 
September 3, 2026  
 
 
The Heritage Commission held its regular monthly meeting in Council Chambers at 37 Green St, on 
Thursday, September 3, 2026.   
 
Members: Vice-Chair Althea Barton, Carol Durgy Brooks, Chair Richard Jaques, City Councilor 
Aislinn Kalob, Jim Spain, and Alternate Member Randall Cotton 
 
Absent:  Michael Dunn and Dr. Bryant Tolles, Jr. 
 
Staff: Matt Walsh, Deputy City Manager – Community Development 
  
  
 
1. Call to Order 
The meeting was called to order by Chair Jaques at 4:30 p.m. 
 
2. Review / Approval of Minutes 
a. July 9, 2026 Regular Meeting 
Member Durgy Brooks moved, seconded by Councilor Kalob, to accept the Heritage Commission 
minutes from July 9, 2026, as submitted. Vice-Chair Barton and Councilor Kalob abstained due to not 
being present at the meeting.  
 
Member Durgy Brooks commented on the meeting minutes in reference to Kimball Jenkins Estate to 
add clarification for the yellow house with the green shutters and the new sign. Part of what the 
Commission requested as a condition was the green outline for Kimball Jenkins that hangs between 
the two windows that the top of the sign be at the same level as the middle sash and the writing says 
green like the shutters. 
 
All in favor. The motion passed. 
b. August 8, 2026 Regular Meeting 
Councilor Kalob moved, seconded by Vice-Chair Barton, to accept the Heritage Commission minutes 
from August 8, 2026, as submitted. Member Durgy Brooks abstained due to not being present at the 
meeting. All in favor. The motion passed.   
3. New Business 
a. Proposed amendments to Code of Ordinances Article 26-9 Demolition Review 
Alternate Member Cotton asked if the 2012 fee of $500 can be increased.  
 
Mr. Walsh noted the legal department with city administration and the only way to amend the charter 
is to take it back to the voters. Mr. Walsh noted state law has a fine of $275.00 a day for the first 
offense or $550 a day for a subsequent offense in RSA 676:17 fines and penalties. This would bring 
the ordinance into compliance. There is a violation established and a penalty.   
 
Member Durgy Brooks asked if there is a way to have the applicant provide a photo with the
Page 2 of 5 
 
application so there is a record of what the building looked like before demolition.  
 
Mr. Walsh stated right now the permit application process does not require photos of the building that 
will be raised. The photos the Commission receives are pictures taken by the code administrator once 
a demolition permit application has been submitted if it is more than 500 square feet or 50 years old 
or modular home. Mr. Walsh noted the Heritage Commission cannot delay the demolition of a 
building there is a 60-day clock on the demolition if the Commission decides to deny the application.  
 
Jennifer Goodman (124 Warren St, Concord) an employee of the New Hampshire Preservation 
Alliance, addressed the Commission during public comment. She noted that stronger remedies—such 
as mandatory reconstruction—would be more likely in the context of a local historic district or a 
preservation easement, and offered to research penalty models used by other communities and share 
them with the Commission. 
 
Mr. Walsh indicated the ordinance would proceed to City Council, with a public hearing anticipated 
in October and potential adoption in November, as the September deadline had already passed. Mr. 
Walsh also confirmed they would note in the staff report to the Council that the Commission supports 
the amendment while encouraging exploration of stronger penalties. 
 
Chair Jaques moved, seconded by Member Durgy Brooks, to approve and recommend to City 
Council the proposed amendments the Code of Ordinances article 26-9, Demolition Review. All in 
favor. The motion passed.  
 
4. Old/Continuing Business 
a. 210 Bog Road Demolition Update 
Mr. Walsh reported that the last communication with the property owner at 210 Bog Road occurred in 
mid-to-late spring, at which time the owner indicated the project would be phased due to rising costs 
and limited financial resources. No further updates have been received.  
 
Chair Jaques noted that no visible activity has been observed at the site. 
b. Master Plan Subcommittee Update  
i. Review Master Plan Subcommittee memorandum 
Vice-Chair Barton presented the Master Plan Subcommittee's memorandum on behalf of the 
subcommittee, which reviewed the Historic Resources section of the current Master Plan and 
condensed its recommendations into a forward-looking document for incorporation into the 
Master Plan 2030. Vice-Chair Barton noted that the subcommittee met multiple times and worked 
diligently to capture existing plan goals rather than introduce wholly new concepts, with the 
intent that ongoing work could be carried forward and continued. 
 
The Commission reviewed the memorandum and proposed the following editorial corrections: on 
page 2, the abbreviation "ag" should be spelled out as "agriculture"; on page 3, the abbreviation 
"PB" should be spelled out as "Planning Board"; and on page 4, the second bullet point 
referencing a framework for Heritage Commission consultation should be revised to read "the 
city, school districts, or the state" (pluralizing "school districts" and adding "either" for clarity) in
Page 3 of 5 
 
order to encompass both Concord and Merrimack Valley school districts, as well as state-owned 
properties within city limits. It was acknowledged that while the state is exempt from municipal 
land use statutes under RSA 674:54 and thus cannot be compelled to seek Heritage Commission 
input, the aspiration to pursue cooperative consultation was seen as worthwhile to retain in the 
plan. 
 
Mr. Walsh commended the subcommittee's work, noting it was significantly ahead of other 
components of the master plan update process. 
 
Councilor Kalob moved, seconded by Member Durgy Brooks, to approve the Master Plan  
Subcommittee memorandum with the noted editorial amendments. All in favor. The motion 
passed.  
 
c. Review Section VIII Historic Resources of the Master Plan 2030 
There was no discussion on this agenda item.  
 
d. Monuments and Granite Markers 
There was no discussion on this agenda item. 
 
5. Heritage Sign Program Review Committee update 
Carol Durgy Brooks reported on three items. First, she noted that the July 9th meeting had approved a 
revision to the Heritage Commission website to add a standing paragraph about the Heritage Design 
Program's semi-annual workshops, directing visitors to the Concord Public Library for sign-up 
information. This was intended to replace a more cumbersome page requiring updates before each 
individual event. As of the meeting date, the revision had not yet been published to the website, despite a 
workshop scheduled for September 8th.  
 
Mr. Walsh acknowledged the oversight, attributing it to the transition in staff support, and committed to 
ensuring the update is made and that a meeting with the returning staff member be arranged upon her 
return in early December to review website maintenance protocols. 
 
Second, Member Durgy Brooks reported that no new sign applications were submitted within the required 
ten business days prior to the meeting, and therefore the September 2nd Heritage Sign Program Review 
Committee meeting was not held. 
 
6. Planning Board Update 
a. Review proposed amendments to Zoning Ordinance Article 28-8 Nonconforming Structures 
Mr. Walsh presented proposed amendments to Zoning Ordinance Article 28-8, specifically Section 
28-8-5(d), which governs the replacement of nonconforming residential structures in the Downtown 
Residential and Urban Transition zoning districts. The primary changes are: (1) shifting jurisdiction 
over such applications from the Zoning Board of Adjustment (via special exception) to the Planning 
Board (via conditional use permit); and (2) adding language specifying that failure of the Heritage 
Commission to provide an advisory opinion within 30 days shall not delay action by the Planning 
Board. Mr. Walsh noted that this provision has rarely, if ever, been invoked during their tenure. The
Page 4 of 5 
 
rationale for moving the process to the Planning Board is that the conditional use permit process 
allows for a more holistic review of a project's site design, whereas the ZBA's special exception 
process is more narrowly focused on satisfying specific criteria. 
 
Vice-Chair Barton and Chair Jaques expressed concern that 30 days is an extremely tight window for 
the Commission to provide meaningful input, particularly given that Commission meetings are held 
monthly and can occasionally be cancelled.  
 
Mr. Walsh acknowledged the concern but explained that the Planning Board itself operates under a 
65-day statutory review period under state law, creating pressure to receive advisory input in a timely 
manner. The open-ended nature of the current process—with no time limit—was the concern that 
prompted planning staff to propose the 30-day clock. Mr. Walsh noted this has already been to 
Planning Board and will go to City Council in September to set a public hearing for October. The red 
items are the changes as to what is being deleted and the blue font is what is being added. Mr. Walsh 
confirmed that the conditional use permit criteria under Section 28-9-3(b) include consideration of the 
master plan's findings, goals, and objectives, as well as input from city boards and commissions, 
though the language is not identical to the special exception criteria. Mr. Walsh clarified that this 
provision applies only to replacement of existing nonconforming structures more or less in kind in the 
two named districts, and is not a vehicle for new construction or significant changes in use.  
 
Member Durgy Brooks left the meeting at 5:45 p.m. 
 
b. Master Plan Update 
i. Project Update 
Mr. Walsh provided an update on the Master Plan 2030 process and referenced the Planning 
Board reports from June 12, July 21, and August 17, 2026 attached to the agenda. 
 
A. June 12, 2026 Report to Planning Board 
B. July 21, 2026 Kick Off Presentation to Planning Board  
C. August 17, 2026 Report to Planning Board 
ii. Master Plan Website: www.concordnh.gov 
Mr. Walsh noted the correct URL for the master plan update page is 
concordnh.gov/masterplanupdate (one word), and clarified an error in the agenda link. 
 
iii. Upcoming Event: Community Visioning Session on September 19, 2026 at 9AM at the Capital 
Center for the Arts 
Mr. Walsh announced that the citywide community visioning session is scheduled for Saturday, 
September 19, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM at the Capitol Center for the Arts. The event 
will include a presentation on the master plan process, data highlights across topic areas including 
historic preservation, and approximately a dozen interactive engagement stations where residents 
can learn about and provide feedback on topics such as housing, transportation, natural resources, 
economic development, and historic resources. Staff expressed hope for an attendance of a few 
hundred participants. The event will be recorded and aired on Concord TV, though it will not be 
broadcast live. The Commission members were encouraged to attend.
Page 5 of 5 
 
iv. Appointment of Planning Board’s Master Plan Advisory Subcommittee 
Mr. Walsh described the Planning Board's decision to form a Master Plan Advisory 
Subcommittee consisting of 15 members: six Planning Board members, one representative and 
one alternate from each of six boards and commissions (including the Heritage Commission), and 
three members of the public. Applications for public members are currently being solicited, with 
nominations from boards and commissions requested by October 14, 2026, so the Planning Board 
may make appointments at its October 21st meeting. The subcommittee is anticipated to meet 
approximately four times during the master plan process. 
 
Chair Jaques requested that the matter of nominating a Commission representative and alternate 
be placed on the October 2026 agenda to allow members additional time to review the 
subcommittee's scope and consider candidates. 
7. City Council Update 
Councilor Kalaob reported that the next City Council meeting is scheduled for September 14, 2026, and 
that no agenda has yet been published. 
 
8. Other Business 
None. 
 
9. Adjourn 
 
Adjournment 
Councilor Kalob moved, seconded by Vice-Chair Barton, to adjourn the meeting at 5:50 p.m. The motion 
passed unanimously. 
 
Respectfully Submitted,  
Krista Tremblay 
Krista Tremblay 
Administrative Technician III 
(Absent from meeting and minutes from recording of the meeting)
